messages:
maria-support: Customer reported: intermittent invalid JSON from /v1/generate when using JSON mode + prefix caching on Dedicated. They see fields from other responses merged into the same object. Example response they pasted:

maria-support: ```
{"id":"resp_a","result":{"name":"Alice","score":0.92}}
{"id":"resp_b","result":{"name":"Bob","score":0.87}}
// actual stream received:
{"id":"resp_a","result":{"name":"Alice","score":0.92}}
{"id":"resp_a","extra":{"name":"Bob","score":0.87}}
```

maria-support: Customer says this started after we rolled out batched-pool config on their Dedicated cluster (pool shard 7). They provided request ids: req=rb_94f1... and req=rb_94f2... and trace id trace=trc-9b2c. Impacting 8% of requests for that customer, causing parse failures in their downstream parser.

tyler-sre: can you paste the original curl they used and whether they used streaming vs non-streaming? also which runtime/version on the dedicated nodes?

maria-support: curl they provided (sanitized):

maria-support: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-large","json_mode":true,"prefix_cache":true,"input":"{\"prompt_id\":1}\n","max_tokens":64}'
```

maria-support: They used streaming: true in their client, but the response chunks combined into invalid JSON once every ~12 requests when their client batches 4 concurrent calls.

raj-eng: can you grab the raw bytes / full stream from our ingress logs for those req ids? need to see whether corruption happens before network egress or in the runtime merge step. also confirm if they were on runtime v2025-11-4 or later.

maria-support: uploaded logs to internal artifact (link: https://artifacts.internal/issue/1951234567/logs) — includes ingress+egress traces and the raw stream for rb_94f1 & rb_94f2. runtime on nodes: v2025-11-6 (we deployed a canary on 11-5).

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: runtime/v2025-11-6 rolled to pool shard-7 @ 2025-11-06T04:12:03Z :rocket:

elena-ml: quick hypothesis: when batching and prefix_cache are both enabled, we might be reusing a KV shard id for different concurrent request prefixes and doing a non-atomic merge of cache entries into the stream buffer. That could produce "shard bleed" where fragments from one response get written under another response's JSON tree. Looks like a race in the prefix stitching path.

tyler-sre: would explain why only occurs with concurrent clients and when max_batch_size>1. can we reproduce by firing two concurrent requests with overlapping prefixes and json_mode true? raj, can you try on a dev node with debug tracing (KV_DEBUG=1)?

raj-eng: yes I'll run repro. steps I'm going to use: 1) start runtime v2025-11-6 on a dev machine with kv_debug=1 and batching enabled 2) run two concurrent POSTs with slightly different input but same prefix key 3) capture stream bytes and trace IDs. sharing script in thread when done.

maria-support: customer also says they saw spike in 504s around the same time. probably retries compounded the mixup. billing note: they flagged this as "blocking" because their parser dropped messages and retried, causing higher token usage.

elena-ml: short-term mitigations: - disable prefix_cache for that customer (tenant override) - set max_batch_size=1 for their pool - flip json_mode to strict parsing server-side to close streams on mismatch. Any of those should reduce risk while we fix the merge atomicity.

maria-support: I applied tenant override: prefix_cache=false for tenant 1234 on shard-7 (will take effect immediately). I've also opened a billing watch to not charge for retries while we investigate.

eng-runtime-oncall: assigned to eng-runtime team. please attach the raw stream traces and the kv debug logs. priority P0 since customer is in production and parser failure is affecting core flow. we suspect a race in the stitcher when multiple batches share shard metadata.

raj-eng: repro script here (dev):

raj-eng: ```bash
for i in 1 2; do 
  curl -s -N -X POST https://dev-runtime.local/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-large","json_mode":true,"prefix_cache":true,"input":"prefix_shared: user prompt '$i'","max_tokens":40}' &
done
wait
```

raj-eng: ran this 1000x and reproduced ~1.2% of the time on dev with the canary runtime. attached logs to the artifact. pattern: partial object from request B written to object A before stream flush.

elena-ml: thanks. next steps for eng-runtime: add an atomic stitch operation or shard-scoped mutex around the prefix stitcher. also add a fast-path for json_mode streams that prohibits cross-request buffer interleaving.

eng-runtime-oncall: noted. i'll create an internal issue and link to this thread, request a hotfix backport to v2025-11-6. can someone capture tcpdump for one repro and upload? we want to be 100% sure it's not network reassembly.

maria-support: i'll ask customer for tcpdump but meanwhile we already have artifacts from ingress which show merged payloads before egress.

tyler-sre: summary: - root cause suspected: race in prefix-cache stitching under batched concurrent streams - immediate mitigations applied: tenant prefix_cache=false, billing watch, optionally set max_batch_size=1 - eng-runtime owning fix and hotfix requested - customer notified and monitoring

maria-support: customer updated that disabling prefix_cache removed the invalid JSON errors. keeping thread open until hotfix lands. :white_check_mark:
